title: Sky light prototype: F12 in the app, four modes
question: Does the pit in panel 2 read as a pit now? And is /4 the one to keep — it is both the cheapest and, unexpectedly, the cleanest?
context_md:
Built and in the app on **F12**, cycling DEPTH (today) → /4 → /2 → /1, named on screen with its cost while it is not the default. `skylight=off|4|2|1` on both `viewshot` and `filmstrip`.

Seeded only where the cell was outdoors at genesis — the per-cell map that shipped last round — then spread at Terraria's 0.91 per air cell / 0.56 per solid, four directional sweeps.

**Two things the design round got wrong, both caught by building it:**

1. I claimed the four-sweep approximation "costs essentially nothing in accuracy" on the strength of sample points agreeing to three decimals. Rendered, one round put a **comb of vertical stripes** down the inside of every pit — the sweeps are separable, so light can go sideways-then-down but never down-then-sideways, and a pit is exactly that shape. Fixed by running the four sweeps twice. The numbers agreed at the points I sampled and the picture disagreed between them.
2. I wrote that the block-grid scan "must not be charged to this approach" because the engine already has occupancy — then implemented it with a `World::get` per cell anyway. Measured **+7.5 ms on a 13.2 ms redraw**, fifty times the prediction. Hoisting the chunk lookup out of the inner loop (a block never straddles a 64-cell chunk) brought it to +2.3 ms.

**Cost, measured and split:** build 1.7 ms + sweep 0.5 ms. Paid **only on frames where the world or camera changed** — which are the frames already doing a full 13 ms redraw. On a settled, still screen it rebuilds **once in 8 frames** and then not at all, so the dirty-rect skip keeps its winnings. That was the explicit worry and it is answered.

**The unexpected result is panel 4.** Finer is not better: at /2 and /1 the striping is still faintly visible, because there is less bilinear blur to hide it. /4 is the cheapest *and* the cleanest — which is Noita's lesson exactly (they fixed their 32x32 fog by blurring, not refining).

Unchanged and checked: shafts still go dark (panel 5), sealed vaults still dark, the overhanging lip still reads as sky.

items.label: 1 — the pit today (DEPTH, unchanged)
items.caption: Dark starts immediately below the cut line and goes flat black. A rectangle, not a hole.

items.label: 2 — /4, what I recommend
items.caption: A bowl of light following the pit's shape: bright at both rims, darkening toward the floor.

items.label: 3 — /2, four times the blocks
items.caption: Faint vertical striping is back near the rim — less bilinear blur to hide the separable-sweep residue.

items.label: 4 — /1, per pixel, the reference
items.caption: Most accurate per the numbers, and visibly the most striped. Kept as the bar, not as a shipping option.

items.label: 5 — shafts under /4: still dark, as you asked
items.caption: 1-, 3- and 8-wide shafts. No sunny sky down any of them — that property comes from the seeding, not the resolution.
